venue: Coors Field (2001 Blake Street, Denver, CO 80205, LoDo). CONFIRMED as the current and only home ballpark of the Colorado Rockies for the 2026 season, and CONFIRMED that the name has NOT changed. (1) Step-0 rename check: a web search for a 2026 naming-rights change returned Denver7 ('Why Coors Field's naming rights won't be changing anytime soon'), Ballpark Digest ('Coors Field Naming Rights Run in Perpetuity', https://ballparkdigest.com/2019/10/31/coors-field-naming-rights-run-in-perpetuity/) and 9News ('Coors doesn't have to pay for "Coors Field" naming rights anymore'), all reporting that Coors Brewing holds the naming rights in perpetuity. Wikipedia states it directly: 'Coors Brewing purchased naming rights "in perpetuity" to the stadium as part of their $30 million investment in the Rockies. A 2017 lease agreement that Rockies club ownership signed with the stadium district ensured that the name would remain at least through 2047.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Field). Ballparks of Baseball lists '-Former Name(s): None', '-Naming Rights: Coors Brewing Company', '-Lease: Through 2047' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/coors-field/). (2) Currency check: the RateYourSeats Coors Field pages carry a full 2026 Rockies home schedule at Coors Field (e.g. 'Aug 17 Mon 6:40pm Los Angeles Dodgers at Colorado Rockies Coors Field - Denver, CO', 'Sep 24 Thu 1:10pm Arizona Diamondbacks at Colorado Rockies Coors Field - Denver, CO') and RYS zone pages are stamped 'Last verified and reviewed: March 2026' and 'Verified Feb 2026'. MLB.com's own 2026 pages are under /rockies/ballpark. No rename, no relocation, no temporary-venue arrangement. NOTE: individual SPACES inside the park have been renamed and re-sponsored (Wells Fargo Club = the 200-level club; PNC Press Club; Toyota Clubhouse, formerly the Infiniti Club; Casamigos Sky Deck, formerly Rio on the Rocks / Captain Morgan Captain's Deck; York Space Systems Suite Level; Legacy Club). Those affect zone NAMES only, not the venue name or the section numbering.
concert_only_sections: Field Sections (concert floor). The RateYourSeats Coors Field section index contains a group 'All Field Seats Sections' whose single entry, 'Field Sections', links to https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/field-seats and is labelled elsewhere on the site as 'Concert Field Seats for Concerts'. That page describes the layout in prose only - 'For concerts, a large stage is typically placed in the outfield, with rows of field seating extending across the infield and toward home plate. ... Some concerts may also include a General Admission (GA) standing section near the front of the field' - and does NOT enumerate any individual concert-floor section labels. No concert-only section IDs can therefore be recorded. Source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/sections ; https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/field-seats

NOTE ALSO: many ordinary baseball sections are flagged by RateYourSeats as concert-limited-view ('105 is behind the stage or to the side of the stage for most concerts', likewise 160, 301, 142, 130 etc.). Those ARE baseball sections and are included in the 'sections' array; the concert warning is view-related only, not a separate section set.
capacity: Conflicting figures, and Ballparks of Baseball is out of date. (1) Wikipedia infobox capacity history: '46,897 (50,144 with standing room) (2018-present) 50,398 (2012-2017) 50,490 (2011) 50,445 (2001-2010) 50,381 (1999-2000) 50,200 (1995-1998)' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Field). (2) Ballparks of Baseball Facts & Figures: '-Capacity: 50,398' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/coors-field/) - this is the SUPERSEDED 2012-2017 figure, predating the 2018 videoboard/seating changes. (3) Ballparks of Baseball narrative also records the design history: 'Originally designed to seat 43,000 fans, the ballpark's capacity was expanded to 50,000 in November 1993 after the Rockies drew an astounding three million fans in their debut season.' (4) Wikipedia also states the Rockpile is a '2,300-seat bleacher section' (Ballparks of Baseball: 'a 2,300-seat bleacher section situated behind the center-field backdrop'), and that Coors Field has 'over 4,400 club seats'. RECOMMENDED: 46,897 (current fixed seating, 2018-present), or 50,144 if a with-standing-room figure is wanted. Do NOT use 50,398.

orientation.batter_faces: NORTH. The batter at home plate looks out toward center field to the north; right field is on the EAST side of the ballpark and left field on the WEST side. The sun rises over right field, curves around home plate around midday and sets behind the left-field stands, which makes the THIRD BASE line the shade side and the FIRST BASE line plus right field the sunny side. This is the reverse of the more common ballpark pattern and matters for any sun/shade text.
orientation.source: https://www.shadedseats.com/coors-field-shaded-seats/ - 'Coors Field is oriented to the north. Every morning, the sun rises over right field. Over the course of the day, it curves around home plate around lunchtime and then dips toward the left field foul pole, eventually setting behind the left field stands. This configuration makes the 3rd base line the "shade side" of the park and the 1st base line and right field the sunny spots.' INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED by the official Rockies Access Guide, which fixes the compass sides via the two ramps: 'There are two access ramps located on the east and west sides of Coors Field. The east ramp can be accessed from Gate A and leads to the Main Concourse, Mezzanine Level and Upper Level. The west ramp can be accessed from Gate E and leads to the Wells Fargo Club, the Suite Level and the Upper Level.' (https://www.mlb.com/rockies/ballpark/disability-access-guide). Gate A is at Section 105 / 'Behind bullpens at Gate A' - i.e. RIGHT FIELD - and is therefore the EAST side; Gate E is at Section 147 - the third-base / left-field-corner side - and is therefore the WEST side. Right field east + left field west => centre field north => batter faces north. FURTHER CORROBORATED by RateYourSeats' own sun language: 'Seats along the third base side will typically experience sunlight earlier during day games, while seats along the first base side tend to remain shaded longer' (Infield Box) and 'Seats on the third base side tend to receive more shade during day games, while seats on the first base side are more exposed to the sun' (Club Level). Ballparks of Baseball gives the site coordinates 39.75620, -104.99402.

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE FROM RIGHT FIELD / THE FIRST-BASE SIDE TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE SIDE / LEFT FIELD. LOW numbers = right field and the first-base side. HIGH numbers = home plate, then third base, then left field. Every numbered series at Coors Field (100s, 200s, 300s) runs the SAME direction; none is reversed. The 400 series (Rockpile, 401-403) is a three-section block in straightaway centre field and does not participate in the sweep. Per-series detail, all sourced: (a) LOWER LEVEL 100s, sections 105-160: 105 is in RIGHT FIELD, immediately beside the home (Rockies) bullpen and just inside Gate A; 105-111 right field; ~112 the right-field corner ('Sit in section 112 (near the right field corner) to be closest to the Blue Moon Brewing Company at the Sandlot'); 114 by the Sandlot Brewery just inside Gate B; 115-120 down the first-base line; 121-125 directly behind the ROCKIES (home) dugout on the FIRST BASE side; 126-135 BEHIND HOME PLATE (with the Toyota Clubhouse field seats in front of them); 136-140 directly behind the VISITOR dugout on the THIRD BASE side; 141-147 down the third-base line (147 is the left-field-corner gate, Gate E); 148-160 LEFT FIELD and LEFT-CENTRE FIELD, ending at 160 with a view of the centre-field waterfall/fountain area. (b) MEZZANINE / CLUB 200s: 201-209 = Right Field Mezzanine, in RIGHT FIELD, with 202-204 sitting directly above the bullpens; 210-213 (no RYS pages) are the Mountain Ranch Club area in the RIGHT FIELD CORNER; 214-227 = Club Level (Wells Fargo Club) running up the FIRST BASE side; 228-233 (no RYS pages) = the suite / press block directly behind home plate; 234-247 = Club Level continuing down the THIRD BASE side. (c) UPPER / RESERVE 300s: 301-309 = Reserve Level Outfield 'on the right field side'; 310-314 = the upper deck behind the Rooftop in right field, 314 near the Blue Moon Brewery on the first-base line; 315-329 up the first-base line and infield; 330-331 BEHIND HOME PLATE (both flagged 'Home Plate View'); 332-336 third-base infield; 338-347 down the third-base line toward the left-field foul pole. (d) LETTERED FIELD-LEVEL SECTIONS A-F = Toyota Clubhouse, directly behind home plate, six rows deep - direction within A-F is NOT stated by any source (see 'uncertain'). INDEPENDENT SYMMETRY CHECK: the official Rockies netting statement, 'Netting runs from the front of Sections 112-147', is symmetric about section 129.5/130, which is exactly where every other source puts home plate. A SECOND independent check: the official Rockies elevator list runs 105 (Gate A, right field) -> 111 (Gate B) -> 130 (Gate D, home plate) -> 147 (Gate E, left-field corner), a monotonic sweep from right field to left field.

anchors.where: RIGHT FIELD (low end of the 100 series). RateYourSeats 'Lower Level Outfield' expert review on the section 105 page: 'Lower Level Outfield seating is located just behind the outfield walls in right, left, and left-center field. ... There are just 14 rows of seating in the right field sections which also have some coverage in the back few rows, while the left field sections contain as many as 23 rows of seating and will have no overhead protection to speak of. Section 105 is a good option for Rockies fans as it is located directly beside the home team bullpen.' Section 105's own row line confirms the right-field row count: 'Rows in Section 105 are labeled 2-14, C-W'. Fan Feedback on the same page: 'The Rockies Bullpen is to the Right of Section 105 - Sit on the right side of Section 105 (closer to seat 1) to be near the Rockies bullpen.' The Rockies bullpens are 'nestled behind the right-field fence' (Ballparks of Baseball), so 105 is unambiguously in right field. Officially corroborated: the Rockies Access Guide lists 'Gate A - Section 105, two (2) elevators' and an escalator 'Behind bullpens at Gate A - to Mezzanine and Upper Level'.

RIGHT-FIELD CORNER and the FIRST-BASE side, low end. RateYourSeats 'Box Level Down the Line' expert review: 'Sit in section 112 (near the right field corner) to be closest to the Blue Moon Brewing Company at the Sandlot, which features a comfortable patio, excellent food and beverage options, and microbrews.' Ballparks of Baseball independently places that brewery in right field: 'the Roundhouse at the Sandlot Brewery (a microbrewery located at the right-field entrance)'. Officially corroborated by the Rockies Access Guide ATM list: 'Inside Gate B - By the Sandlot Brewery, near section 114' and the elevator list 'Gate B - Section 111, one (1) elevator'.

FIRST BASE SIDE - behind the HOME dugout. RateYourSeats Infield Box: 'Prime Dugout Views: Sections 121-125 sit behind the Rockies dugout, while 136-140 sit behind the visitor dugout.' and, in the body, 'Sections 121-125 sit directly behind the Rockies dugout, while Sections 136-140 are positioned behind the visitor dugout.' Ballparks of Baseball states the home dugout side outright: '-Home Dugout: First Base'. Therefore 121-125 (low) = first base, 136-140 (high) = third base: numbers increase toward third base.

BEHIND HOME PLATE, lower level. RateYourSeats Infield Box: 'It's important to note that the sections behind home plate (126-135) do not extend all the way to the field, as the Toyota Clubhouse seating occupies the field-level area directly in front of those sections.' RateYourSeats section 130 Seating Notes: 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate' and the expert note 'Incredible views of the action from right behind home plate. Great perspective to the batters box and on-deck circles.' Officially corroborated three ways: the Rockies elevator list has 'Gate D - Section 130, two (2) elevators' (Gate D is the home-plate gate); the Guest Relations Center and assistive-listening desk are 'across from section 127'; and the official netting run 'Sections 112-147' is symmetric about 129.5.

THIRD BASE SIDE and the third-base line. RateYourSeats Infield Box: 'Sections 136-140 are positioned behind the visitor dugout.' RateYourSeats 'Box Level Down the Line' (on the section 142 page): 'Sit near the top (Rows 32 and higher) of sections 142-147 to minimize the walk to concessions and restrooms, and you'll also be rewarded with great overhead coverage and excellent shade.' - and ShadedSeats independently establishes that the shade side at Coors is the THIRD BASE side, so a shade recommendation for 142-147 places them on the third-base side. Officially corroborated: 'Gate E - Section 147, (1) elevator', 'Inside Gate E - Near section 147', and 'The west ramp can be accessed from Gate E' (west = the left-field/third-base side, per the orientation entry).

LEFT FIELD / LEFT-CENTRE FIELD (high end of the 100 series). RateYourSeats section 160 row line: 'Rows in Section 160 are labeled 2-23' - matching the expert review's statement that 'the left field sections contain as many as 23 rows of seating' while 'There are just 14 rows of seating in the right field sections'. Fan Feedback on section 160: 'You have a view of the fountains when the Rockies hit a home run. - It is really a very pretty center field park and from this section you can see the stream that runs through it and the water fall.' ShadedSeats independently groups them as outfield: 'Outfield sections 151-160 and center field sections 401-403 are sun-exposed and receive almost no shade during the day' and 'Outfield sections 151-160 will receive some shade once the sun dips behind the stadium' (which only works if 151-160 are on the west/left-field side).

RIGHT FIELD, mezzanine level - low end of the 200 series. RateYourSeats Right Field Mezzanine: 'Second-Tier Outfield Seating: Located in Sections 201-209 in right field on the mezzanine level.' and 'The Right Field Mezzanine consists of Sections 201 through 209 and sits on the second tier of seating in right field at Coors Field.' and 'Bullpen Views: Sections 202-204 sit directly above the team bullpens.' Officially corroborated: the Rockies escalator list has 'Section 201 - to Upper Level' immediately after 'Behind bullpens at Gate A'.

CLUB LEVEL DIRECTION CONFIRMATION. RateYourSeats Club Level: 'Club Level seats are located on the second tier of Coors Field, running from the first base side through the third base side in Sections 214-227 and 234-247.' Read with the 100-series (121-125 = Rockies dugout = first base) and with the escalator 'Section 218 - to Suite Level', the low block 214-227 is the FIRST BASE side and the high block 234-247 is the THIRD BASE side. Officially corroborated: the Rockies ATM list places 'Wells Fargo Club - Near section 234'. RateYourSeats also notes 'Two Full-Service Bars near Sections 221 and 236' - a symmetric pair straddling the 228-233 gap, i.e. one bar per side.

RIGHT FIELD, upper/reserve level - low end of the 300 series. RateYourSeats 'Reserve Level Outfield' expert review, quoted verbatim on the section 301 page: 'Reserve Level Outfield is the highest tier of outfield seating on the right field side of Coors Field. Home run balls this high up are a rarity even in the thin air of the Rocky Mountains. Sun exposure will be some of the heaviest in these seats. Center field seats will have a tough viewing angle to the videoboard, and fans closer to the right field corner will stay closer to the Blue Moon Brewery down the first base line.' (ShadedSeats confirms right field is the sunny side at Coors, so 'heaviest sun exposure' is itself consistent with right field.)

RIGHT FIELD, upper level, behind/beside The Rooftop, running toward the first-base line. RateYourSeats Rooftop Tickets: 'The Rooftop is located in the upper level in right field, occupying a large portion of the stadium above the outfield seating.' and 'Rooftop tickets are typically general admission standing-room tickets, but for some games fans may also be able to access Sections 310-314 for seating.' RateYourSeats 'Reserve Level Down the Line': 'Scoreboard watchers get a better angle to the left field videoboard from the first base side, and will also be closer to Blue Moon Brewery (near Section 314).' - fixing 314 on the FIRST BASE side. ShadedSeats agrees: 'Seats in the upper-level 300 sections along the 1st base line also receive little shade during the early innings.'

BEHIND HOME PLATE, upper/reserve level. RateYourSeats section 331 Section Insights list 'Home Plate View'; its Seating Notes read 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'; and a verified fan review on that page reads 'We had seats in the upper deck, right behind home plate. We were in row 10, which is the first row after the walkway in the upper deck.' RateYourSeats section 330 likewise carries the 'Home Plate View' insight and 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'. The two neighbours 327 and 328 carry the 'Reserve Level Infield' review but NOT the behind-home-plate note. Officially corroborated: the Rockies list an ATM 'Behind section 330 - Clocktower area' (the Coors Field clock tower stands at 20th & Blake, the home-plate corner of the ballpark) and a First Aid Station 'behind sections 133 and 330' - 133 being a lower-level home-plate section, so 133 and 330 are a stacked home-plate pair. ShadedSeats independently recommends 'the upper rows in sections 330-335' as the upper-level equivalent of the lower-level home-plate shade block 'sections 128-135'.

THIRD BASE LINE toward the LEFT-FIELD foul pole - high end of the 300 series. RateYourSeats 'Reserve Level Down the Line' expert review on the section 347 page: 'Sitting on the Reserve Level between the corner bases and the foul poles will leave you with some of the furthest views for a Rockies game at Coors Field. Seats on the first base side will see a heavy dose of sun during day games, so fans looking for shade are advised to consider the third base side (sun will be at your back earlier).' Section 347's rows are labelled '10-23', matching the deep left-side geometry rather than the shallow right-field upper deck.

STRAIGHTAWAY CENTRE FIELD - a self-contained block, not part of the left/right sweep. RateYourSeats Rockpile Seats: 'Center Field Bleachers: Located beyond the center field wall, offering a straightaway view of the field.' and 'Because the Rockpile sits in straightaway center field, it is also the furthest seating area from home plate in the stadium.' Wikipedia: 'The center field bleacher section is named "The Rockpile". ... is located in deep center field up high.' and 'The very last section of seats are 600 feet away from home plate, making them the furthest away from home plate in any MLB stadium.' ShadedSeats names the sections: 'Outfield sections 151-160 and center field sections 401-403 are sun-exposed'. Officially corroborated: the Rockies elevator list includes 'Rockpile - Underneath the Rockpile in center field, one (1) elevator'.

numbering_direction.confidence: very high. Four fully independent source families agree and none dissents: (1) the official Rockies Access Guide for Guests with Disabilities on mlb.com, whose gate/elevator/escalator/ramp listings sweep monotonically 105 -> 111 -> 130 -> 147 from right field to left field and whose east/west ramp statement independently fixes the compass sides; (2) the official Rockies netting page, whose stated run 'Sections 112-147' is symmetric about 129.5, exactly the section pair every other source calls home plate; (3) RateYourSeats zone pages (Infield Box, Club Level, Right Field Mezzanine, Rockpile, Rooftop, Toyota Clubhouse, Press Club, Legacy Club, Mountain Ranch Club) plus a dozen individual section pages; (4) ShadedSeats.com's sun/shade geography and Ballparks of Baseball's '-Home Dugout: First Base'. No source anywhere places section 105 or 301 in left field, or 160 or 347 in right field.

home_plate_sections.Club Level / Wells Fargo Club (200 level: NONE - this tier does NOT wrap behind home plate. RateYourSeats states the tier explicitly as two separate blocks: 'Club Level seats are located on the second tier of Coors Field, running from the first base side through the third base side in Sections 214-227 and 234-247.' Sections 228-233 are absent from the range and absent from the RateYourSeats venue section index; the space directly behind home plate on this tier is occupied by the suite / press block (the Legacy Club sits 'behind home plate on the York Space Systems Suite Level' and the PNC Press Club sits 'directly behind home plate on the Lower Press Level'). The two full-service club bars, 'near Sections 221 and 236', straddle that gap symmetrically. Configure NO home-plate anchor for the 200-level Club Level.
home_plate_sections.Right Field Mezzanine (200 level, sectio: NONE - outfield-only area. 'Located in Sections 201-209 in right field on the mezzanine level.' It never reaches the infield, let alone home plate.
home_plate_sections.Casamigos Sky Deck (Mezzanine Level, sec: NONE - outfield-only area. 'The Casamigos Sky Deck is located on the Mezzanine Level in center field at Coors Field. ... Tickets are sold in Sections 200A-200C and feature reserved seating along railings overlooking right-center field.'
home_plate_sections.Mountain Ranch Club (200 level): NONE - right-field-corner-only area. 'The Mountain Ranch Club is located on the 200 Level in the right field corner at Coors Field.' (Ballparks of Baseball describes the equivalent space as 'the Mountain Ranch Club, which offers fine dining across six tiers along the right-field line.')
home_plate_sections.Rooftop (upper level, right field): NONE - right-field-only standing/social area. 'The Rooftop is located in the upper level in right field, occupying a large portion of the stadium above the outfield seating.' Mostly general-admission standing room; sections 310-314 are sometimes opened for seating, and those are right-field/first-base-line sections, not home-plate sections.
home_plate_sections.Rockpile (400 level, sections 401-403): NONE - outfield-only bleacher block in straightaway centre field. 'Because the Rockpile sits in straightaway center field, it is also the furthest seating area from home plate in the stadium.' The Rockpile must NEVER be given a home-plate anchor.

levels.name: Toyota Clubhouse (field level, directly behind home plate) - lettered sections A-F
levels.sections: A, B, C, D, E, F (RateYourSeats slugs club_a ... club_f; the venue section index labels them 'Club A' ... 'Club F')
levels.notes: 'Closest Seats to Home Plate: Located in Sections A-F, with every seat within about six rows of the field.' / 'Toyota Clubhouse seating is located directly behind home plate in Sections A-F at field level. This seating area places fans closer to the action than anywhere else in the stadium.' / 'All seats sit within roughly six rows of the field, making them the closest seats to home plate at Coors Field. Seats in this area also feature extra padding and premium chair designs.' / 'Fans access their seats through the tunnel behind home plate, giving a unique perspective similar to what the umpires see when they take the field.' All-inclusive pregame buffet (alcohol NOT included), in-seat wait service, private entrance. Formerly the Infiniti Club (the RYS seating-chart asset is still named infiniti-cub-seating-chart-for-rockies-games-at-coors-field.jpg). These field-level seats sit in FRONT of lower-bowl sections 126-135, which is why 'the sections behind home plate (126-135) do not extend all the way to the field'. Only Club A has a photo on RateYourSeats; B-F have none, and NO row labels or seat counts are published for any of A-F.

levels.name: Lower / Box Level (100 level) - sections 105-160
levels.sections: 105-160 (contiguous; RateYourSeats has no pages for 101-104 and a request for /sections/103 redirects to the section index, so on RYS the series begins at 105)
levels.notes: The main lower bowl. RateYourSeats splits it into three named zones. INFIELD BOX (the lower-bowl infield): 'Closest Infield Seating: Located on the lowest tier behind home plate and the dugouts for an up-close view of the action.' / 'Prime Dugout Views: Sections 121-125 sit behind the Rockies dugout, while 136-140 sit behind the visitor dugout.' / 'Large Sections: Up to 38 rows per section' / 'Rows in these sections typically feature about 14 seats per row, and some sections extend up to 38 rows deep.' / 'Concourse Access in Higher Rows: Rows 20 and higher are closer to the concourse tunnels.' / 'Fans sitting in the last few rows (Row 32 and higher) in Sections 120-127 and 134-141 can benefit from overhead protection provided by the 200-level seating deck above.' BOX LEVEL DOWN THE LINE: 'Still located on the lowest tier of the field but further down the line, these Box Level seats are the best place to be on the Coors Field seating chart for catching a foul ball. ... The sections have a large number of rows (with as many as 38 numbered seating rows), which makes for a long walk up to the concourse for fans in the closest rows. Sit near the top (Rows 32 and higher) of sections 142-147 ... Sit in section 112 (near the right field corner) to be closest to the Blue Moon Brewing Company at the Sandlot.' LOWER LEVEL OUTFIELD: 'Lower Level Outfield seating is located just behind the outfield walls in right, left, and left-center field. While most of the seats are exposed to a good amount of sun for most day games, they are also the best place to sit at Coors Field to catch a home run ball. There are just 14 rows of seating in the right field sections which also have some coverage in the back few rows, while the left field sections contain as many as 23 rows of seating and will have no overhead protection to speak of. Section 105 is a good option for Rockies fans as it is located directly beside the home team bullpen.'

levels.notes: RIGHT FIELD MEZZANINE: 'Second-Tier Outfield Seating: Located in Sections 201-209 in right field on the mezzanine level.' / 'Smaller Sections: No more than 17 rows per section' / 'Bullpen Views: Sections 202-204 sit directly above the team bullpens.' / 'Fans looking for some relief from the sun should consider Rows 5 and higher in sections closer to the right field corner.' CLUB LEVEL (officially the Wells Fargo Club): 'Elevated Views: Located on the second tier of Coors Field (Sections 214-227 and 234-247) with excellent sightlines of the field.' / 'Short Sections: No more than 13 rows per section' / 'Exclusive Club Concourse: Climate-controlled hallway with premium concessions and full-service bars.' / 'Two Full-Service Bars near Sections 221 and 236' / 'Shade in Higher Rows: Rows 8 and higher benefit from overhead coverage from the deck above.' / 'The best covered seats are typically found in Rows H and above' (note: this 'Rows H' phrasing conflicts with the numeric row labels actually published for club sections - see 'uncertain'). Section 241 page: 'Rows in Section 241 are labeled 1-10, W', 'An entrance to this section is located at Row W'. MOUNTAIN RANCH CLUB: 'Right Field Corner Location: Located on the 200 Level in the right field corner with an elevated view of the field.' / 'Reserved Table Seating: Tables for two or four guests'. CASAMIGOS SKY DECK: 'The Casamigos Sky Deck is located on the Mezzanine Level in center field at Coors Field. This area sits just below The Rooftop ... levels.name: Suite Level (York Space Systems Suite Level) and Lower Press Level - Legacy Club and PNC Press Club
levels.sections: Suite Club 1, Suite Club 2 (Legacy Club); Press Club 1, Press Club 2, Press Club 3 (PNC Press Club). All five are zone-only entries on the RateYourSeats index - they link to the zone page, not to individual section pages - so no per-section geometry exists.
levels.notes: LEGACY CLUB: 'Behind Home Plate Location: Located on the York Space Systems Suite Level directly behind home plate.' / 'The Legacy Club is located behind home plate on the York Space Systems Suite Level at Coors Field. This premium area is sometimes referred to as the Suite Club and sits just above the lower seating bowl.' / 'Small Private Sections: Each section features two rows of seats plus a rail row (Row R).' / 'Indoor / Outdoor Experience: Climate-controlled lounge with retractable glass windows that open to the field.' PNC PRESS CLUB: 'Behind Home Plate Location: Three premium sections located directly behind home plate on the Lower Press Level.' / 'The PNC Press Club is located directly behind home plate on the Lower Press Level at Coors Field. This premium seating area consists of three small sections' / 'Rows 1-2: Traditional padded stadium seats with comfortable spacing. Row R: Padded bar-style seats located along a rail' / 'Open-Air Press Level Views: Retractable windows allow the space to feel open-air while maintaining indoor comfort.' The Rockies' own escalator list references this tier: 'Section 218 - to Suite Level'. These tiers exist only behind home plate and should be given NO left/right sweep.

levels.name: Upper / Reserve Level (300 level) - sections 301-347
levels.sections: 301-319, 321, 323, 325-336, 338, 340, 342-347 as listed on the RYS index (320, 322, 324, 337, 339 and 341 have no RYS section page)
levels.notes: RESERVE LEVEL INFIELD (verbatim, repeated on sections 321, 325, 327, 328, 330, 331): 'The Reserve Level is located on the highest tier of the inner seating bowl at Coors field. These Infield oriented sections will have more aerial views from behind home plate and the dugouts. Rows closest to the front of these sections are referred to as Lower Reserved (with up to 10 rows of seating), while the back rows are known as the Upper Reserved (up to 15 rows of seating). Sit in rows 19 and above to take advantage of the overhead coverage and be near the purple seats (the mile high mark), or in Rows closer to the front to be near the concourse entry tunnel.' RESERVE LEVEL OUTFIELD (section 301): 'Reserve Level Outfield is the highest tier of outfield seating on the right field side of Coors Field.' RESERVE LEVEL DOWN THE LINE (section 347): 'Sitting on the Reserve Level between the corner bases and the foul poles will leave you with some of the furthest views for a Rockies game at Coors Field.' Typical row labelling on this level is a split pattern: 'Rows in Section 331 are labeled 1-5, C-W, 10-25' (Lower Reserved 1-5, then lettered/accessible rows, then Upper Reserved 10-25), with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 5'. A verified fan review for section 331 explains the break: 'We were in row 10, which is the first row after the walkway in the upper deck. As the seats were raised up above the walkway, we had a totally unobstructed view of the game.' Seat counts vary within a section: for 330, 'In the lower portion of Section 330 (Rows 1-5), there will be 14 to 15 seats in each row (with fewer seats in the rows near the front). In the upper portion of the Section (Rows 10 and higher), the seats will range between 17 to 24 in each row with more seats in the rows near the back of the section.'

levels.name: The Rooftop (upper level, right field) - general admission, plus sections 310-314 on select dates
levels.sections: No dedicated section numbers; the RYS index lists a single zone entry 'Rooftop'. Sections 310-314 (300 level) are sometimes released as seating for Rooftop ticket holders.
levels.notes: 'Massive Social Gathering Space: A 38,000-square-foot standing-room area' / 'The Rooftop is located in the upper level in right field, occupying a large portion of the stadium above the outfield seating. The area spans roughly 38,000 square feet and features a two-tier design' / 'Rather than traditional stadium seating, the Rooftop is built as a social plaza with standing room, bar rails, and communal spaces' / 'Rooftop tickets are typically general admission standing-room tickets, but for some games fans may also be able to access Sections 310-314 for seating. This additional seating is not guaranteed and is usually announced on the day of the game depending on attendance levels.' A fan review is filed under 'Rooftop / Row G14', showing that Rooftop tickets can carry lettered-plus-number row codes. Ballparks of Baseball gives the history: 'In October 2013, the Rockies unveiled plans for a major renovation of the upper deck in right field. By the start of the 2014 season, most of the upper deck seating in right field had been replaced with a two-level rooftop deck.'

levels.name: The Rockpile (400 level) - sections 401, 402, 403
levels.notes: 'Most Affordable Seating Area: The Rockpile is widely known as the most budget-friendly seating option at Coors Field.' / 'Center Field Bleachers: Located beyond the center field wall, offering a straightaway view of the field.' / 'Classic Bleacher Seating: Bench-style seating without back support.' / 'Rockpile seating is located beyond the center field wall at Coors Field. These sections sit above the outfield concourse and feature a bleacher-style layout rather than individual stadium chairs. Seats here do not have seat backs' / 'Because the Rockpile sits in straightaway center field, it is also the furthest seating area from home plate in the stadium.' / 'Located just below the seating area is Dinger's Playground, found inside the Platte River Rendezvous section of the stadium. This play area is designed for children 42 inches tall and under.' / 'For day games, fans should be aware that these seats are fully exposed to the sun with little overhead protection.' Wikipedia: 'The center field bleacher section is named "The Rockpile". ... The original Rockpile seats cost a dollar each.' and 'The very last section of seats are 600 feet away from home plate, making them the furthest away from home plate in any MLB stadium.' Ballparks of Baseball: 'a 2,300-seat bleacher section situated behind the center-field backdrop'. Section 401 has a photo captioned 'Section 401, Row 15'. THIS TIER NEVER REACHES HOME PLATE - see home_plate_sections.

dugouts.home: FIRST BASE SIDE. Ballparks of Baseball Facts & Figures states it plainly: '-Home Dugout: First Base' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/coors-field/). Independently corroborated by RateYourSeats Infield Box, twice on the same page: 'Prime Dugout Views: Sections 121-125 sit behind the Rockies dugout, while 136-140 sit behind the visitor dugout.' and 'Sections 121-125 sit directly behind the Rockies dugout, while Sections 136-140 are positioned behind the visitor dugout.' Since 121-125 are the low-numbered (right-field/first-base) side of the home-plate block, the Rockies dugout is on the first-base side. A third, weaker corroboration: the home (Rockies) bullpen is beside section 105 in right field, on the same side of the diamond as the home dugout.
dugouts.visiting: THIRD BASE SIDE. RateYourSeats Infield Box: 'Sections 136-140 are positioned behind the visitor dugout.' / '136-140 sit behind the visitor dugout'. 136-140 are the high-numbered (third-base/left-field) side of the home-plate block.

bullpens: BOTH bullpens are beyond the RIGHT-FIELD fence, in front of the landscaped 'mountain' area. Ballparks of Baseball: 'The bullpens are nestled behind the right-field fence, adjacent to a landscaped area featuring trees, rocks, water fountains, and a mountain-inspired scene. Adding a personal touch, the Rockies' relievers maintain a small garden near their bullpen.' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/coors-field/). RateYourSeats Right Field Mezzanine: 'Bullpen Views: Sections 202-204 sit directly above the team bullpens.' and 'One unique feature of this area is that Sections 202-204 sit directly above the team bullpens, giving fans a chance to watch pitchers warm up during the game.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/right-field-mezzanine). RateYourSeats 'Lower Level Outfield' review: 'Section 105 is a good option for Rockies fans as it is located directly beside the home team bullpen.' RateYourSeats Fan Feedback on section 105: 'The Rockies Bullpen is to the Right of Section 105 - Sit on the right side of Section 105 (closer to seat 1) to be near the Rockies bullpen.' Officially corroborated by the Rockies Access Guide escalator listing: 'Behind bullpens at Gate A - to Mezzanine and Upper Level' (Gate A is the Section 105 / right-field gate). SO: the HOME (Rockies) bullpen is the one immediately adjacent to section 105, on the side of section 105 toward lower seat numbers / toward right-centre. The exact home-vs-visitor left/right order of the two bullpens, and whether they are side-by-side or stacked, is NOT stated by any source consulted - record as UNKNOWN.

special_areas.name: Toyota Clubhouse (formerly the Infiniti Club)
special_areas.where: Field level, sections A-F directly behind home plate; every seat within roughly six rows of the field; private entrance; access via the tunnel behind home plate; all-inclusive pregame buffet (no alcohol) and in-seat wait service; extra-padded seats
special_areas.level: Field level (in front of lower-bowl sections 126-135)

special_areas.name: Legacy Club (a.k.a. Suite Club)
special_areas.where: Directly behind home plate on the York Space Systems Suite Level, just above the lower bowl; Suite Club 1 and Suite Club 2; each section has two seating rows plus a rail row 'R'; climate-controlled lounge with retractable glass windows; all-inclusive buffet plus select beer and wine

special_areas.name: PNC Press Club
special_areas.where: Directly behind home plate on the Lower Press Level; three small sections (Press Club 1, 2, 3); Rows 1-2 padded stadium seats plus Row R padded rail seats; retractable windows; all-inclusive buffet plus select beer and wine; private entrance

special_areas.name: Club Level (Wells Fargo Club)
special_areas.where: Second tier, sections 214-227 (first base side) and 234-247 (third base side); no more than 13 rows per section; climate-controlled private concourse; two full-service bars near sections 221 and 236; in-seat wait service; Rows 8+ covered

special_areas.name: Mountain Ranch Club (Mountain Ranch Bar & Grille)
special_areas.where: 200 Level in the RIGHT FIELD CORNER; reserved dining tables for two or four overlooking the field, plus an adjacent indoor club dining space with a premium buffet. Ballparks of Baseball describes it as 'fine dining across six tiers along the right-field line'

special_areas.name: Right Field Mezzanine
special_areas.where: Sections 201-209, second tier in right field; no more than 17 rows per section; 202-204 sit directly above the bullpens; heavy sun exposure; Rows 5+ nearer the right-field corner get some overhead cover

special_areas.name: Casamigos Sky Deck (formerly Rio on the Rocks / the Captain's Deck)
special_areas.where: Mezzanine Level in centre field, just below The Rooftop; sections 200A, 200B, 200C; reserved rail seating overlooking right-centre field; full-service bar directly behind; floor-to-ceiling glass panels; sunset views over the Rockies and the downtown skyline

special_areas.name: The Rooftop
special_areas.where: Upper level in RIGHT FIELD; a 38,000 sq ft two-tier standing-room social plaza with bar rails, cabanas, an urban-garden environment and many TVs; Coors Light Silver Bullet Bar, Smashburger, Jack Daniel's Terrace Bar, 5280 Craft Bar, CHUBurger, VIP Cabana Terrace; sections 310-314 sometimes opened for seating

special_areas.name: The Rockpile
special_areas.where: Sections 401-403, bleachers beyond the centre-field wall above the outfield concourse; bench seating with no seat backs; roughly 2,300 seats; the cheapest tickets in the park and the furthest seats from home plate in MLB (~600 feet)

special_areas.name: Dinger's Playground / Platte River Rendezvous
special_areas.where: Directly below the Rockpile seating area, in the Platte River Rendezvous section of the ballpark; designed for children 42 inches tall and under

special_areas.name: Blue Moon Brewing Company at The Sandlot (the Roundhouse at the Sandlot Brewery)
special_areas.where: Right-field entrance, near section 112 and inside Gate B near section 114; a working microbrewery with a patio; the Rockies A-Z guide lists a liquor bar at 'section 112 at Blue Moon Brewing Co.'; on the upper deck it is nearest section 314
special_areas.level: Main concourse, right field / first base line

special_areas.name: Clock tower
special_areas.where: At 20th and Blake Street, the home-plate corner of the ballpark; a popular pregame meeting spot; the Rockies list an ATM 'Behind section 330 - Clocktower area' and a liquor bar at 'section 330 at the Clocktower'
special_areas.level: Exterior / upper-level concourse behind home plate

special_areas.name: The purple mile-high row
special_areas.where: Row 20 of the upper deck, all the way around; Wikipedia: 'While most of the seats in Coors Field are dark green, the seats in the 20th row of the upper deck are purple to mark the [one mile above sea level elevation]'; Ballparks of Baseball: 'A row of purple seats encircles the upper deck, marking one mile above sea level.' RateYourSeats ties it to a row recommendation: 'Sit in rows 19 and above to take advantage of the overhead coverage and be near the purple seats (the mile high mark)'

special_areas.name: Landscaped 'mountain' area / fountains beyond the outfield fence
special_areas.where: Beyond the centre/right-centre outfield wall behind the bullpens; trees, rocks, water fountains and a mountain-inspired scene; a fan in section 160 reports 'you can see the stream that runs through it and the water fall'

special_areas.name: Main videoboard and out-of-town scoreboard
special_areas.where: Ballparks of Baseball: 'The main HD video scoreboard is located beyond the left-field bleachers, while a 14-foot-tall out-of-town scoreboard is embedded in the right-field wall.' The 2018 board measures '59 feet high by 116.5 feet wide' with a rock-shaped top edge
special_areas.level: Beyond the left-field bleachers / in the right-field wall

special_areas.name: Guest Relations Center
special_areas.where: Main concourse across from section 127; issues assistive listening devices, resolves ticket issues and assists guests with disabilities to their seats

accessibility.summary: From the official Colorado Rockies 'Access Guide for Guests with Disabilities' (https://www.mlb.com/rockies/ballpark/disability-access-guide), verbatim where quoted. ACCESSIBLE SEATING: 'There are approximately 1,000 accessible and companion seats available throughout Coors Field.' / 'Line of sight: All accessible seating is either front row or provides line of sight to the playing field and scoreboard over standing patrons. Access to front row seating is via elevators and ramps with a travel distance comparable to other front row seating for ambulatory spectators.' / 'Coors Field is accessible through all five entry gates (A-E). At Gates A & E, guests using wheelchairs may use the ramp or elevator to reach all levels. Entry at Gates B, C & D is on the main concourse level and ramps and elevators are available to reach all levels.' The guide names NO specific accessible section numbers - unlike several other clubs, the Rockies publish a count and a policy but not a section list. PARKING: 'Approximately 300 disabled parking spaces are available immediately adjacent to Gate A, in the front of Lot A. Lot A is paved, lit and fenced in. ... Through Gate A, elevators, ramps, stairs and escalators provide access to the various levels of Coors Field.' RAMPS: 'There are two access ramps located on the east and west sides of Coors Field. The east ramp can be accessed from Gate A and leads to the Main Concourse, Mezzanine Level and Upper Level. The west ramp can be accessed from Gate E and leads to the Wells Fargo Club, the Suite Level and the Upper Level. The grade on both ramps conforms to ADA standards.' WHEELCHAIR STORAGE: wheelchairs are stored at Guest Services on four different levels for guests who transfer to a seat. BRAILLE: 'There are signs in braille at our restroom locations.' ASSISTIVE LISTENING: 'The Guest Relations Center has devices which can assist Guests who have hearing/visual impairments. Please stop by the Center at section 127 for more information. AM Radio - Games are announced on 850KOA.' CAPTIONING: 'The closed caption board is located under the main scoreboard and will display text transcribed from P.A. announcements. A limited number of text display devices will be available at the Guest Relations Center (section 127) for Guests who do not have a view of the main scoreboard.' GUEST SERVICES: 'During every event, Guest Relations Center is located on the main concourse across from section 127.' Phone 303-ROCKIES (303-762-5437). FAN TEXTING: text 'SECURITY' plus the issue and location to 97475. BAGS: 'Coors Field regulations allow only soft-sided bags and containers 16"x 16"x 8" or smaller to be permitted in the gates.'
landmarks: GATES - five entry gates, A through E. Gate A is the right-field gate at Section 105, adjacent to Lot A and the accessible parking; Gate B is at Section 111 by the Sandlot Brewery (ATM 'Inside Gate B - By the Sandlot Brewery, near section 114'); Gate C is near Section 123 (ATM 'Inside Gate C - Near section 123'); Gate D is the home-plate gate at Section 130; Gate E is the third-base / left-field-corner gate at Section 147 (ATM 'Inside Gate E - Near section 147')

ELEVATORS (official list, verbatim) - 'Gate A - Section 105, two (2) elevators / Gate B - Section 111, one (1) elevator / Gate D - Section 130, two (2) elevators / Gate E - Section 147, (1) elevator / Rockpile - Underneath the Rockpile in center field, one (1) elevator'

ESCALATORS (official list, verbatim) - 'Behind bullpens at Gate A - to Mezzanine and Upper Level / Section 201 - to Upper Level / Sections 122 and 147 - to Wells Fargo Club / Section 218 - to Suite Level / Sections 123 and 147 - to Upper Level (up only)'

RAMPS - east ramp from Gate A (right field) to Main Concourse, Mezzanine Level and Upper Level; west ramp from Gate E (third base / left-field corner) to the Wells Fargo Club, the Suite Level and the Upper Level

FIRST AID - 'The First Aid Station at section 133 is open two hours prior to every game. The First Aid Station at section 330 will be open during select games.' / 'First Aid Stations are located behind sections 133 and 330.' (133 = lower level behind home plate; 330 = upper level behind home plate - a stacked home-plate pair, useful as a symmetry check)
GUEST RELATIONS CENTER - main concourse across from section 127; also the assistive-listening and captioning-device pickup point

ATMs (six) - 'Inside Gate B - By the Sandlot Brewery, near section 114 / Inside Gate C - Near section 123 / Inside Gate E - Near section 147 / Wells Fargo Club - Near section 234 / Behind section 306 - The Rooftop, next to Fan Accomodations / Behind section 330 - Clocktower area'
TEAM STORE / NOVELTY - 'Majestic Team Store - Section 149'; 'Novelty - Sections 110, 120, 147, 158, 226, 330'; 'Diamond Dry Goods - Section 116'

GLUTEN-FREE / SPECIAL DIET STANDS (useful as additional left/right landmarks) - 'Gluten Free - Sections 111, 142'; 'Infield Greens Salad - Section 120, Mountain Ranch'; 'Veggie Burger and Dog - Section 134, 323'; 'Buckaroos - A concession stand for kids ... Section 149'; 'CHUBurger - Section 303'

PAIRED CONCESSION LANDMARKS spanning levels (independent symmetry evidence) - 'Extreme Dog - Sections 130, 144, 331'; 'Fanfare (hot dogs) - Sections 109, 119, 128, 139, 157, 312, 318, 327, 338, 344, 401, 403'; 'Portable Grills - Sections 107, 117, 142, 147, 157, 311, 321, 341'; 'Colorado Craft Beers - Sections 121, 136, 151, 327'
ACCESSIBLE PARKING - approximately 300 spaces in Lot A immediately adjacent to Gate A (right field), $18.00 per vehicle on the day of the game, price subject to change

row_seat_conventions: ROWS: a MIXED system - numbers, letters, and at some sections a split numeric range with a lettered block in between. Everything below is verbatim from the named RateYourSeats section page unless attributed otherwise. LOWER / BOX LEVEL (100s): 'Rows in Section 105 are labeled 2-14, C-W' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row W'; 'Rows in Section 130 are labeled 4-38, C-W' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row W'; 'Rows in Section 142 are labeled 1-38, C-W' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row W'; 'Rows in Section 160 are labeled 2-23' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 23'. So the lower bowl generally runs numbered rows from the field back, then a lettered block C through W behind them, with the section entrance at the LAST lettered row (W) - i.e. fans enter from the TOP of the section and walk down. RateYourSeats notes the consequence: sections have 'as many as 38 numbered seating rows, which makes for a long walk up to the concourse for fans in the closest rows', and 'Rows 20 and higher are closer to the concourse tunnels'. Note that lower-bowl numbered rows do NOT all start at 1 (105 starts at 2, 130 at 4, 160 at 2). CLUB LEVEL (200s): 'Rows in Section 241 are labeled 1-10, W' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row W'; the Club Level zone page says 'No more than 13 rows per section' and 'Rows 8 and higher benefit from overhead coverage', but ALSO says 'The best covered seats are typically found in Rows H and above' - a lettered reference that does not match the published numeric labels (flagged in 'uncertain'). RIGHT FIELD MEZZANINE (201-209): 'No more than 17 rows per section.' UPPER / RESERVE LEVEL (300s): a distinctive SPLIT pattern - 'Rows in Section 321 are labeled 1-5, C-W, 10-25'; 'Rows in Section 327 are labeled 1-5, C-W, 10-25'; 'Rows in Section 331 are labeled 1-5, C-W, 10-25'; 'Rows in Section 328 are labeled 1-5, C, 10-25'; 'Rows in Section 330 are labeled 1-5, C, 10-25'; 'Rows in Section 325 are labeled 1-25'; 'Rows in Section 301 are labeled 1-5, W'; 'Rows in Section 347 are labeled 10-23'. RateYourSeats explains the split: 'Rows closest to the front of these sections are referred to as Lower Reserved (with up to 10 rows of seating), while the back rows are known as the Upper Reserved (up to 15 rows of seating)', and a verified fan review for 331 adds 'We were in row 10, which is the first row after the walkway in the upper deck.' Entrance rows on the 300 level are typically Row 5 (321, 327, 328, 330, 331) or Row 6 (325) or Row 10 (347) - i.e. at the bottom of the Upper Reserved block, NOT at the very top. ROCKPILE (401-403): bleacher benches, 'Bench-style seating without back support'; a section 401 photo is captioned 'Row 15'. PREMIUM TIERS: Toyota Clubhouse 'every seat within about six rows of the field' (no row labels published); PNC Press Club 'Rows 1-2: Traditional padded stadium seats ... Row R: Padded bar-style seats located along a rail'; Legacy Club 'Two traditional seating rows' plus 'A third rail row labeled "R" positioned behind the seats'. ROOFTOP: a fan review is filed as 'Rooftop / Row G14'. ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION: the label 'WC' IS used at Coors Field, and lettered rows C-W sit at the accessible/concourse break. Evidence: RateYourSeats section 142 Section Insights read 'Top Pick for Outstanding Convenience Rows 36-WC' and its Seating Notes read 'For baseball games, we recommend rows 36-WC for outstanding convenience' - so 'WC' is a row identifier that sorts after row 36 and after the lettered rows. On the upper level RateYourSeats says explicitly, for sections 328 and 330, 'There is wheelchair seating betweeen Rows C and 10' [sic - RYS's own typo], i.e. the wheelchair platform sits between the lettered row C and Upper-Reserved row 10. The RYS Q&A for section 105 refers to 'the handicap seating at the very top of the section'. No 'WCH', 'VWC' or 'AC' suffix was found anywhere, and the official Rockies guide does not state any row-label convention - so beyond 'WC' and the C-W lettered block, treat accessible-row labelling as UNKNOWN. SEATS: see seat1_side_verbatim.
seat1_side_verbatim: RateYourSeats states, IDENTICALLY on every Coors Field section page checked: "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the right". Verified verbatim, character for character, on these ten section pages: 105 (https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/sections/105), 130, 142, 160, 241, 301, 321, 325, 327, 328, 330, 331 and 347. NOTE THE DIRECTION CAREFULLY: at Coors Field the sentence says "on the RIGHT", which is the OPPOSITE of what RateYourSeats says at several other parks in this project (e.g. every Citi Field section page reads "...lower number seats are on the left"). Do not copy the Citi Field wording. The 'right' answer is given uniformly regardless of where the section sits: in right field (105, 301), behind home plate (130, 330, 331), on the first-base side (321, 327, 328 all sit in the infield sweep), on the third-base side / down the third-base line (142, 347), on the club level (241) and in left field (160). RateYourSeats therefore treats seat numbering at Coors Field as running uniformly RIGHT-to-LEFT as the fan faces the field, i.e. seat 1 is always the rightmost seat in the row from the fan's perspective. CORROBORATION: a Fan Feedback note on section 105 uses the same convention and ties it to a physical landmark - 'The Rockies Bullpen is to the Right of Section 105 - Sit on the right side of Section 105 (closer to seat 1) to be near the Rockies bullpen.' - explicitly equating 'the right side' with 'closer to seat 1'. NO CONTRADICTING SOURCE was found: neither the official Rockies Access Guide, nor Ballparks of Baseball, nor Wikipedia, nor ShadedSeats states any seat-numbering rule for Coors Field, and no guide was found asserting the common alternative rule ('seat 1 is closest to home plate'). Confidence in the seat-1 side is therefore HIGH, resting on twelve identical RateYourSeats statements plus one independent fan corroboration, but it rests on a single source FAMILY (RateYourSeats).
known_obstructions: PROTECTIVE NETTING - OFFICIAL TEAM STATEMENT (prefer this): the Colorado Rockies' own Coors Field seating-chart page states, in full, 'Netting runs from the front of Sections 112-147.' (https://www.mlb.com/rockies/ballpark/netting). That run is symmetric about section 129.5/130 and reaches from the right-field corner (112) to the left-field corner (147). CONFLICTING THIRD-PARTY FIGURE: RateYourSeats carries a fan-feedback note repeated across Coors Field section pages (seen on section 130) reading 'Front of sections 122-139 are behind the netting - There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 122-139. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section.' The RateYourSeats range (122-139) is much narrower than the official range (112-147) and is almost certainly the pre-2018/pre-2020 dugout-to-dugout netting; a 2018 Rockies announcement reported by MLB.com and roxpile said the netting would be 'extended at the same height to the end of each dugout', and a later report said the club would 'evaluate all options to extend netting at Coors Field for the 2020 season'. Both ranges are recorded; USE 112-147 and flag the conflict. UPPER-DECK WALKWAY - on the 300 level the Lower Reserved rows (1-5) are separated from the Upper Reserved rows (10-25) by a walkway; a verified fan review for section 331 reports that this is a BENEFIT not an obstruction, because 'As the seats were raised up above the walkway, we had a totally unobstructed view of the game the entire time' from row 10, the first row after the walkway. SIGHTLINE / SCOREBOARD LOSS - RateYourSeats 'Reserve Level Outfield' (section 301): 'Center field seats will have a tough viewing angle to the videoboard'; 'Reserve Level Down the Line' (section 347): 'Scoreboard watchers get a better angle to the left field videoboard from the first base side.' The main videoboard is 'beyond the left-field bleachers' (Ballparks of Baseball) so left-field and centre-field seats have the worst angle to it. TOYOTA CLUBHOUSE BLOCKS THE FRONT OF 126-135 - RateYourSeats Infield Box: 'the sections behind home plate (126-135) do not extend all the way to the field, as the Toyota Clubhouse seating occupies the field-level area directly in front of those sections.' LONG WALKS RATHER THAN OBSTRUCTIONS - lower-bowl sections run up to 38 numbered rows with the entrance at the top (Row W), 'which makes for a long walk up to the concourse for fans in the closest rows'. SUN AS THE PRACTICAL 'OBSTRUCTION' AT COORS - ShadedSeats: 'Although some lower-level right field seats may be shaded if they're under cover, these locations are still less than ideal, as fans will have to contend with the sun positioned in a way that it shines directly in their eyes during the game.' NO source consulted reports support poles or structural columns anywhere at Coors Field. CONCERT-ONLY VIEW LIMITS (not baseball obstructions): RateYourSeats flags many sections with 'X is behind the stage or to the side of the stage for most concerts' - seen on 105, 160 and 301.
uncertain: THE RATEYOURSEATS SECTION INDEX IS NOT A COMPLETE LIST OF PHYSICAL SECTIONS - HIGH PRIORITY. The 'sections' array above is taken exhaustively from https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/sections, exactly as instructed, and contains 139 entries. But RateYourSeats' own zone pages name sections that the index omits. Specifically the Club Level page says the tier runs 'in Sections 214-227 and 234-247', yet the index has no pages for 220, 224, 237 or 240 - so those four club sections almost certainly exist physically but have no RateYourSeats page and are therefore NOT in the array. Similarly the 300 series jumps 319 -> 321 -> 323 -> 325 and 336 -> 338 -> 340 -> 342, so 320, 322, 324, 337, 339 and 341 have no RateYourSeats page; whether they exist physically is NOT established by any source consulted. Downstream phases must decide whether to synthesise these ten section IDs or leave them out; do not assume the index gap means the section does not exist.

LOWER-LEVEL SECTIONS 101-104. The RateYourSeats index begins the 100 series at 105, and a direct request for https://www.rateyourseats.com/coors-field/seating/sections/103 REDIRECTS to the section index (i.e. no such page). No source consulted states whether physical sections 101-104 exist at Coors Field. They are excluded from the array. If they do exist they would be further into right/right-centre field than 105, i.e. even lower-numbered and even deeper toward the bullpens - which would not change the numbering DIRECTION.

EXACT HOME-PLATE CENTRE ON THE LOWER LEVEL. RateYourSeats says the behind-home-plate block is '126-135' (arithmetic midpoint 130.5) while the official Rockies netting run '112-147' is symmetric about 129.5. Section 130 is chosen as the single anchor because it is the only one of the two candidates that carries the RateYourSeats note 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate', and because the Rockies place two elevators and Gate D at Section 130. 129 or 131 would be defensible alternatives; the SIDE is certain, the exact centred section number is medium confidence.

EXACT HOME-PLATE CENTRE ON THE UPPER LEVEL. Both 330 and 331 carry the RateYourSeats 'Home Plate View' insight and the 'desirable view from behind home plate' note, and 331 additionally has a verified fan review saying 'right behind home plate'. Neighbours 327 and 328 do NOT carry the note. ShadedSeats, however, describes the upper-level home-plate shade block as 'sections 330-335', which would push the centre a little higher. Both 330 and 331 are recorded as the anchor pair. Medium-high confidence in the pair, high confidence in the side.

THE 200-LEVEL 'NONE' RULING. The claim that the Club Level does not wrap behind home plate rests on one explicit RateYourSeats sentence ('running from the first base side through the third base side in Sections 214-227 and 234-247'), on the absence of 228-233 from the RateYourSeats index, and on the fact that the Legacy Club (Suite Level) and PNC Press Club (Lower Press Level) both sit 'directly behind home plate' on adjacent tiers. No official Rockies document was found that says outright that club sections 228-233 do not exist. If a later source shows 228-233 are ordinary club seats, the 200-level home-plate anchor would be roughly 230/231.

MOUNTAIN RANCH CLUB SECTION NUMBERS. RateYourSeats says the Mountain Ranch Club is 'located on the 200 Level in the right field corner' but gives it a single unnumbered index entry. The 200-series index gap between 209 (last Right Field Mezzanine section) and 214 (first Club Level section) is 210-213, which is exactly where a right-field-corner club would sit, but NO source states that the Mountain Ranch Club occupies sections 210-213. That mapping is an INFERENCE and is flagged as such. Note also that Ballparks of Baseball describes the club as running 'across six tiers along the right-field line', which is a slightly different description from RateYourSeats' 'right field corner'.

TOYOTA CLUBHOUSE SECTION ORDER (A through F). RateYourSeats says only that the six lettered sections are 'directly behind home plate' with 'every seat within about six rows of the field'. It does NOT say which end is the first-base end and which the third-base end, does not name a centred section, and does not publish row labels or seat counts for any of A-F (only Club A has a photo). By analogy with every numbered series at this park, A would be expected at the first-base/right-field end and F at the third-base/left-field end, but NO source states this. Do not generate seat-1 or side statements for A-F without further evidence.

LEGACY CLUB AND PRESS CLUB SECTION GEOMETRY. Suite Club 1-2 and Press Club 1-3 are zone-only entries on the RateYourSeats index - every one links to the zone page rather than to an individual section page - so no per-section left/right ordering, row labels beyond 'Rows 1-2' and 'Row R', or seat counts exist. They are EXCLUDED from the 'sections' array. Give them a home-plate flag but no directional sweep.

CASAMIGOS SKY DECK SECTIONS 200A-200C. Named in prose on the zone page ('Tickets are sold in Sections 200A-200C') and listed as three index entries, but all three link to the zone page, not to individual section pages. No rows, no seat counts, no left/right ordering. Excluded from the 'sections' array. Note also that RateYourSeats describes the location inconsistently within one page: 'located on the Mezzanine Level in center field' in one sentence and 'overlooking right-center field' / 'close to the social spaces in right field' in others.

ROOFTOP GEOMETRY. The Rooftop is a single unnumbered index entry and is 'typically general admission standing-room'. A fan review is filed under 'Rooftop / Row G14', implying some lettered-plus-number row coding exists, but no row scheme is published. Sections 310-314 are 'sometimes' released as Rooftop seating; whether they should be treated as Rooftop or as ordinary 300-level Reserve sections is not settled.

CLUB-LEVEL ROW LABELS CONFLICT. The RateYourSeats Club Level zone page says 'Fans looking for overhead protection should aim for Rows 8 and higher' and then 'The best covered seats are typically found in Rows H and above' - but the only club section page with published labels, section 241, reads 'Rows in Section 241 are labeled 1-10, W'. There is no Row H in that list. Either the club sections have a lettered block that RateYourSeats does not enumerate on the individual pages, or the 'Rows H' sentence is boilerplate carried over from another venue. Unresolved.

NETTING RANGE CONFLICT. Official Rockies: 'Netting runs from the front of Sections 112-147.' RateYourSeats fan-feedback note: 'There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 122-139.' Both recorded verbatim in known_obstructions; the official 112-147 is recommended, and the RateYourSeats figure is believed to be stale (pre-2018 dugout-to-dugout netting). A 2018 report said the netting would be 'extended at the same height to the end of each dugout', and a later report said the club would 'evaluate all options' for 2020; no source found states the exact current top-of-net height by section.

CAPACITY. 46,897 (Wikipedia, 2018-present) vs 50,144 (Wikipedia, with standing room) vs 50,398 (Ballparks of Baseball, which is the superseded 2012-2017 figure) vs the historical series 50,490 / 50,445 / 50,381 / 50,200. Ballparks of Baseball is out of date on this field and should not be used. 46,897 recommended.

BULLPEN OWNERSHIP AND ARRANGEMENT. Both bullpens are behind the right-field fence and sections 202-204 sit 'directly above the team bullpens'. RateYourSeats places the home (Rockies) bullpen beside section 105 and a fan note says it is 'to the Right of Section 105 ... closer to seat 1'. But no source states whether the two bullpens are side-by-side or stacked, nor which is nearer the foul line - record the relative order as UNKNOWN.

COMPASS ORIENTATION rests on one explicit statement ('Coors Field is oriented to the north', ShadedSeats.com) plus an inference from the official Rockies east/west ramp assignment (east ramp = Gate A = right field; west ramp = Gate E = left-field/third-base corner). No official Rockies or Wikipedia sentence giving a compass bearing was found. Confidence is high because two independent sources agree, but note that the resulting sun geography is UNUSUAL for MLB - at Coors the THIRD BASE side is the shade side and the FIRST BASE side is the sunny side, which is the reverse of most parks. RateYourSeats independently confirms this reversal twice ('Seats along the third base side will typically experience sunlight earlier during day games, while seats along the first base side tend to remain shaded longer' on the Infield Box page, and 'Seats on the third base side tend to receive more shade during day games, while seats on the first base side are more exposed to the sun' on the Club Level page) - note these two RateYourSeats sentences are themselves slightly inconsistent with each other about WHEN the third-base side is sunny, so use ShadedSeats for any sun/shade text.

PURPLE MILE-HIGH ROW - SINGLE-ROW CLAIM. Wikipedia says 'the seats in the 20th row of the upper deck are purple to mark' the one-mile elevation, and Ballparks of Baseball says 'A row of purple seats encircles the upper deck, marking one mile above sea level.' RateYourSeats agrees loosely ('Sit in rows 19 and above ... to be near the purple seats (the mile high mark)'). But the 300-level row labels are split (1-5, C-W, 10-25), so it is NOT established whether 'the 20th row' means the row LABELLED 20 or the twentieth physical row counting from the front. Flag before generating any purple-row seat statement.
